Name: Community Mod Chest
Author: Jared
Description: A collection of community-suggested content additions. Includes new apparel, weapons and armor, character-creation traits (including a Founders Kit starter bundle — a cabin kit, two rain cistern kits, and a stockpile of building materials, all unpacked from one portable kit — and a standalone Extra Rain Cistern Kit perk for more cisterns; the mod's other former starter building-kit perks now live in the separate HomesteadPerks mod), pottery and sculpting items, comfort items, fishing gear, village content east of the River Clearing (cross by building the River Bridge, or swim the river at a steep cost in stamina and arrive soaked and weary; strong swimmers cross more easily), a Clay Mound for digging clay, a Market Stall for selling trade goods, an enterable Village Inn with a Town Achievement Board that tracks eleven achievements, and an enterable Village Academy with seven courses, including a Carpentry course that unlocks an Outfit Wardrobe (three separate 18-slot sections, one per outfit -- hang gear in a section, then Equip or Unequip that whole outfit in one motion instead of swapping pieces by hand) and a Wicker Chair. The Village supports long-form civic growth through buildable homes, a Village Hall whose Reputation meter starts at a true neutral and rises toward its ceiling only once every tracked building project AND every villager errand is complete (also visible as a Mental attribute in your character menu), and a Boards room with seven notice boards: Village Standing, Village Projects, and one board each for the Inn Keeper, Miller, Weaver, Apothecary, and Professor. The villager boards now open directly to their notices without redundant read actions and track active errands, hints, teasers, relationship standing, and recent errand history. Includes the village timeline, resident move-ins, a daily Miller/Weaver schedule (home in their own enterable cottage overnight, working the grindstone or the loom in the village by day — restocking their own trade goods as they go — a nightly Inn visit, and one Academy day every week — each with matching Inn/Academy card art), the Inn Keeper friendship and lost-cat storyline, the Professor's errands and milestone gifts, the Herbalism-gated Apothecary's Cabin with her own nightly Inn visit and weekly Academy day (also with matching card art), and Shadow the Cat as a separate tameable companion. The Inn Keeper and Professor react, once each, to village construction milestones (new cottages, the Village Hall, Village Reputation thresholds) and, for the Professor, to each Academy course you pass. A communal Town Wood Pile stands in the village square: stock it with twigs, sticks, wood or firewood to keep the six village hearths burning, or let it run dry and watch those fires go out — stocking also builds a separate Player's Pay balance you can withdraw any time as copper nuggets or salt, a reward for the fuel you contributed that never touches what the hearths need. Every winter, snow drifts block all three roads out of the Village until dug clear with a shovel. Four Town Watch guards -- Captain Reeve Sterling, Nella Thorne, Old Corrin and the night-shift Iris Vane -- take up posts around the village with three distinct jobs. Thorne and Corrin walk the Town Square by day and attack any thief or attacker they catch on village ground; Iris Vane keeps the night watch but, once your crimes brand you an enemy of the village, hunts you down anywhere on the map, day or night, and calls the rest of the Watch in rather than fighting you herself -- unlike the other three, village borders do not stop her. Talk to Captain Sterling and he gives you one formal warning the first time your standing turns Suspected -- and once you're Wanted, any guard who spots you reacts without a fight, watching you more closely, while a conversation with the Captain turns visibly colder. Any of them can be attacked, at a steep and immediate Village Crime cost; guards usually break and flee rather than die, but killing one brands you Banished for good. The Watch is no pushover: all four carry real Blood and armor well beyond a starting-gear brawler's reach, and Captain Sterling hits hardest of all -- winning against a fresh, unequipped character is not the expected outcome. A landed hit leaves a real mark: it raises Bruising alongside Fear and drops an actual wound item -- a Bruise, Abrasion, Laceration, or Puncture depending on severity -- into your inventory that needs Cleaning (or, for the worse ones, Stitching) to stop hurting. Only one guard fights you at a time, so a cornered criminal takes them on back to back, and a guard you nearly beat stays wounded into the next fight; killing one outright (rather than just breaking their morale) is a steep and separate hit to your Village Crime on top of the cost of starting the fight. Best all four and the charges do not drop on their own -- the Inn Keeper hears what happened before you tell her, and only a private conversation owning up to it actually clears your name. A guard you merely rout is out of the Watch for a season before returning to their own post; a guard you kill outright is gone for just a week, and comes back standing in the Village Jail rather than at their old post. Losing to Thorne or Corrin gets you held, not jailed on the spot -- they pin you down and send for the Captain, and Sterling would rather talk you down than fight: he offers to take you in peacefully and lets you walk away up to three times before he stops asking and simply takes you in unhurt, with no Bruising. Attack him yourself instead, or let the whole Watch converge on you at once, and he does not hold back -- he fights for real, harder than any of the other three. Either way, the Watch has you: you wake up in the Village Jail beside the Village Hall, serving a sentence set by what you did -- at least 3 days for any arrest, 7 days for every guard you killed since your last full sentence (capped at 8), or roughly a day for every 8 points of crime if you never spilled blood -- with no way out of the cell until the sentence is served -- a meager daily ration of gruel and water keeps you alive without letting you thrive, backed by an emergency top-up if you ever get dangerously hungry, thirsty, or underweight, and Meditate, Sleep, and a stone-counting distraction help pass the time. Guards take turns standing warden on the jail step, in four non-overlapping shifts that cover the whole day between them, and every so often the whole Watch is off the step at once -- and during that rare gap, the cell's own bed can be shoved aside to dig at a hidden tunnel underneath. Get caught digging with the tunnel still exposed and the sentence grows and the tunnel caves back in; finish digging and crawling through clears the remaining sentence, gets you out past the walls, and marks you as an escaped convict -- worse to be caught again. All five named villagers keep a Copper Chest in their own interior -- the Miller's and Weaver's cottages, the Apothecary's Cabin, the Inn, and the Academy. Each adds salt and a little of their own trade stock to it weekly, up to a per-NPC ceiling: the Inn Keeper is the richest buyer in the village, the Miller and Weaver sit mid-tier, and the Apothecary and Professor keep thinner purses but rarer goods. You can sell valuable items to any of them, paid out of that chest's actual contents (so each can only afford what they have actually saved), or rob a chest instead if you are willing to risk being caught by its owner or the night watch. These are personal savings -- the Inn's till and the Academy's tuition account are separate and unaffected. Once the Weaver's regular errands are all done, she has one last thing to teach you: a Climbing Rope pattern, sturdy enough to anchor on the cliff face north of Sett Warren. Fix one there and the path down to Greenfalls opens both ways -- previously impassable in either direction. A Clay Ocarina lets any player craft their own way to tame Shadow the Cat. The Academy Medicine course now grants a craftable payoff (Herb Poultice, Herb Tincture), and Old Growth Bark tans hides into leather. New flavor craftables round out the mod: a Toys & Games line (Bone Dice, Spinning Top, Wheeled Horse), Pigment-dyed apparel variants, a Scented Candle, a Cat Bed with a treat interaction for all three cats (their descriptions now show Care-tier flavor text as it rises and falls), and two new starting traits (Potter's Apprentice, Caravan Peddler). A new Quiet Village trait trades away roaming village content for reduced simulation overhead: the Miller, Weaver, Apothecary, and Professor stay home, at the Academy, or at the Inn instead of commuting or foraging, and none of the four Town Watch guards take up their posts at all. The Copper Chests now tie into Trust and Village Crime: selling into any of the five chests raises that resident's Trust, dragging Salt or a Metal Nugget onto the Miller's chest pays down crime as restitution, a Burglar's Kit shaves a little off a chest search's detection odds, and the Town board now shows a soft, tiered read of your standing with the village. The three non-Sterling Town Watch guards (Thorne, Corrin, Vane) now have a friendly Talk option of their own, the Market Stall can toggle a cosmetic awning, village interiors work like a cabin room (Insulation, Cabin Fever, 200 Comfort; buildable Windows, and a buildable Fireplace in the Jail Cell), an autumn deadfall now blocks the Pine Trail route in season alongside the winter snow drifts, and a spring thaw floods the Clay Shoal ford -- wait the water down on the bank, or build the new Plank Causeway at Clay Shoal and lay it across to open the road at once.
